newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Oilseeds - Korea to buy Brazilian beans, meal.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - Korea to buy Brazilian beans, meal.

text.p: South Korean buyers were seen seeking more soybeans and soymeal from Brazil instead of the U.S. due to its attractive offer prices, traders said on Monday.
Shindongbang Corp is seeking 50,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans for July/August shipment, a company official said.

Other South Korean feed millers may also pickup about 80,000 tonnes of Brazilian soymeal this week for September/October arrival, a trader with a Seoul-based foreign trading house said. South Korean feed millers would continue to buy feed for June/September arrival, the trader added.

The National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) has already invited bids for 45,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellets, 20,000 tonnes of rice bran pellets and 18,000 tonnes of cottonseed meal on Tuesday.
Two South Korean soybean crushers, Cheiljedang Corp and Sam Yang Foods Co Ltd, last Thursday bought 50,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans for July shipment from Japanese trading house Marubeni Corp.
In Japan, oilseed importers have almost finished buying U.S. soybeans for July shipment, but some are baulking at further purchases due to concerns about overbuying, traders said.
"Our buying for July shipment is almost over. We'd like to watch the market's next direction," an official at a major soybean crusher said.
A soybean trader said rising prices on the Chicago Board of Trade may be a cause for worry among Japanese importers.
"But we remember overbuying of U.S. corn last year, and are hesitant to buy," the soybean trader said.
